answer: We run Google Ads for Rusty Pelican in Miami and Tampa and built its website. In 2025, every $1 of Miami ads brought back about $7 in tracked bookings.

paragraphs: Big waterfront rooms live on reservations, private events and holiday rushes.
In two very different markets, Miami and Tampa, every ad dollar has to show what it brought back.

items.title: Reach people who are already looking
items.bodyHtml: Google search ads aimed at people already searching for a place to eat, with every click tracked through to the booking.

items.title: Split the goals
items.bodyHtml: Separate campaigns for reservations, private events and seasonal dates, with private events as the focus in Tampa.

items.title: Plan around the big dates
items.bodyHtml: Seasonal pushes for days like Mother's Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas, when people book ahead.

items.title: Track every booking
items.bodyHtml: Conversion tracking on calls, reservations and form fills, reported against spend every month.

items.title: Build the website
items.bodyHtml: We designed and built the Rusty Pelican site: full-bleed photography, a menu by section, the chef's story and reservations wired in. More on our restaurant website design page.

results.explainHtml: How to read these numbers: a conversion is one tracked action, like a reservation, a call or a private-event inquiry. ROAS (return on ad spend) compares the tracked value of those conversions with what the ads cost.

accounts.name: Rusty Pelican Miami
accounts.standout: Mother's Day brought 155 conversions at $3.06 each. Thanksgiving brought 252 at $3.70 each.
